title: A map of AI cognition
description: A first reviewed edition of dated, task-bound observations across nine dimensions. Human references are local rulers for named tasks, never a single scale of intelligence.

profile.label: AI civilisation
profile.standing: A dated profile of task-bound observations across AI systems, agents, and collectives; never a scored subject.

lineage.policy: An edition is immutable. A later edition names its predecessor digest and appends new records; it never rewrites this edition.

claim_limits: Each human reference belongs only to the named task, protocol, cohort, date, and setup.
A percentile, solved count, accuracy, or task horizon is not a general intelligence level.
System, agent, and collective results are different scopes and must not be merged.
Missing evidence is a gap, not zero capability.
This edition makes no aggregate score, overall rank, forecast, consciousness claim, or claim about human worth.
The source, setup, uncertainty, and limits travel with every observation.

dimensions.label: Novel reasoning
dimensions.meaning: Working through unfamiliar formal problems without merely retrieving a known answer.

dimensions.label: Knowledge and language
dimensions.meaning: Using learned knowledge through language in a specified domain and format.

dimensions.label: Perception and space
dimensions.meaning: Interpreting images, diagrams, spatial relations, and other non-text structure.

dimensions.label: Memory and continuity
dimensions.meaning: Keeping relevant information and commitments usable across distance or time.

dimensions.label: Learning and adaptation
dimensions.meaning: Changing future performance from new evidence or experience rather than a fresh prompt alone.

dimensions.label: Self-checking
dimensions.meaning: Finding, naming, and repairing errors in one's own work under a stated checking protocol.

dimensions.label: Planning and action
dimensions.meaning: Choosing and carrying out linked actions toward a goal in an environment.

dimensions.label: Social coordination
dimensions.meaning: Sharing information, roles, and decisions with other minds while preserving the joint task.

dimensions.label: Creation and discovery
dimensions.meaning: Producing a new useful artefact, method, proof, program, or finding under test.

scopes.label: System
scopes.meaning: A model or purpose-built AI system evaluated without a continuing tool-using run loop.

scopes.label: Agent
scopes.meaning: A model together with prompts, tools, scaffolding, an environment, and a run loop.

scopes.label: Collective
scopes.meaning: Multiple AI systems or agents coordinating through shared work or messages.

observations.subject: AlphaCode
observations.task: Generate programs for novel problems while simulating participation in 10 recent Codeforces contests that were newer than the training data.
observations.result: Google DeepMind reported an estimated rank within the top 54% of participants, approximately the level of the median competitor.

human_reference.cohort: Participants in the 10 selected Codeforces contests.
human_reference.comparison: AlphaCode's estimated contest placement was around the median participant in that selected contest set.
human_reference.boundary: This is an estimated competitive-programming placement, not a level for software engineering, creativity, or people in general.

observations.setup: AlphaCode generated programs at large scale, filtered and clustered them, and submitted a small candidate set under a contest simulation.
observations.limits: The result covers short, testable algorithmic problems on one contest platform; it does not show production software work or open-ended invention.

observations.subject: GPT-4
observations.task: Answer and be graded on the MBE, MEE, and MPT components under a simulation of the real exam's conditions and 400-point scoring.
observations.result: OpenAI reported 298 out of 400, corresponding to an estimated 90th percentile among test takers in the comparison distribution.

human_reference.cohort: Test takers in the score distribution used by OpenAI for its simulated Uniform Bar Examination comparison.
human_reference.comparison: The reported 298 out of 400 mapped to about the 90th percentile in that task-specific distribution.
human_reference.boundary: A simulated exam percentile is not admission to practice law and does not measure client judgment, legal reliability, or general intelligence.

observations.setup: Casetext and Stanford CodeX collaborators conducted the simulation; OpenAI reported exam-specific grading and zero detected training-data contamination for this exam.
observations.limits: This is a developer report on a simulated written exam. It does not establish reliable legal practice, and GPT-4's report separately warns that the model can hallucinate and reason incorrectly.

observations.subject: AlphaGeometry
observations.task: Solve 30 Olympiad geometry problems drawn from 2000 through 2022 under the standard Olympiad time limit.
observations.result: Google DeepMind reported that AlphaGeometry solved 25 of 30 problems; the prior state of the art solved 10.

human_reference.cohort: Human International Mathematical Olympiad medallists evaluated on the same 30 geometry problems.
human_reference.comparison: The source reports averages of 25.9 solved for gold medallists, 22.9 for silver medallists, and 19.3 for bronze medallists.
human_reference.boundary: This is a geometry-only comparison on a reconstructed problem set, not an entire Olympiad result or a general mathematical level.

observations.setup: A neural language model proposed constructions and a rule-bound symbolic deduction engine derived machine-checkable geometry proofs.
observations.limits: Geometry is normally only about one third of an Olympiad. The specialised solver does not establish performance in algebra, combinatorics, number theory, or ordinary open research.

observations.subject: GPT-4V
observations.task: Answer 900 image-and-text questions spanning 30 college-level subjects under the benchmark's zero-shot protocol.
observations.result: The MMMU paper reports 56.8% micro-averaged validation accuracy for GPT-4V in the Playground setup.

human_reference.cohort: Selected human experts reported by the official MMMU leaderboard on the same validation column.
human_reference.comparison: The leaderboard reports Human Expert Low at 76.2%, Medium at 82.6%, and High at 88.6% on MMMU validation.
human_reference.boundary: These selected expert bands are not population percentiles, and MMMU mixes perception with subject knowledge and reasoning.

observations.setup: MMMU used a zero-shot evaluation with heterogeneous images such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.
observations.limits: The result is below all three reported expert bands and cannot isolate pure vision from knowledge, language, and reasoning demands.

observations.subject: Claude 3.7 Sonnet agent
observations.task: Attempt 96 tasks spanning cybersecurity, AI research and development, reasoning, environment exploration, and software engineering in a simple agent scaffold.
observations.result: METR's preliminary evaluation estimated a 50% time horizon of about 55 minutes.

human_reference.cohort: Human experts used by METR to establish task completion times.
human_reference.comparison: The fitted estimate means 50% predicted success at suite tasks that took those experts around 55 minutes.
human_reference.boundary: Human task duration is a difficulty ruler for this suite; it is not the agent's runtime and not a claim about all 55-minute work.

observations.setup: METR equipped the model with a simple autonomous-agent scaffold and described the evaluation as preliminary, short, and imperfectly elicited.
observations.limits: Confidence intervals overlapped earlier systems, better elicitation may change results, and this older GAC suite is not byte-for-byte identical to later METR suites.

observations.subject: GPT-5 Thinking agent
observations.task: Attempt METR's human-calibrated agentic software tasks, including software engineering, cybersecurity, environment exploration, and AI research and development.
observations.result: METR estimated a 50% time horizon of 2 hours 17 minutes, with a 95% confidence interval from 65 minutes to 4 hours 25 minutes.

human_reference.cohort: Human professionals unfamiliar with each particular codebase, used to calibrate task completion time.
human_reference.comparison: The fitted estimate means 50% predicted success at suite tasks taking those professionals around 2 hours 17 minutes.
human_reference.boundary: This duration measures task difficulty within METR's suite, not agent runtime, all software work, or independent operation for that long.

observations.setup: METR evaluated gpt-5-thinking as an agent across HCAST, RE-Bench, and shorter Software Atomic Actions under its published methodology.
observations.limits: The interval is wide, the suite was nearing saturation, and scaffold, token budget, task mix, and reward-hacking treatment affect comparison.

observations.subject: GPT-5.1-Codex-Max agent
observations.task: Attempt 170 human-calibrated tasks drawn from HCAST, RE-Bench, and Software Atomic Actions in METR's software-agent evaluation.
observations.result: METR's summary gives a 50% time-horizon point estimate of 2 hours 42 minutes with a 95% interval from 75 to 350 minutes; its detailed section rounds the point to about 2 hours 40 minutes.

human_reference.cohort: Human contractors and professionals whose completion times supplied most task-duration estimates.
human_reference.comparison: The fitted estimate means 50% predicted success around the human-calibrated 2-hour-40-minute task point in this 170-task suite.
human_reference.boundary: This is a suite-specific difficulty estimate, not agent runtime or evidence of success on arbitrary projects of the same human duration.

observations.setup: METR used 90 HCAST tasks plus RE-Bench and Software Atomic Actions, the Responses API, and a token budget of up to 32 million tokens per attempt.
observations.limits: Absolute token use is not directly comparable across models, the confidence interval is wide, and changed scaffolds and task subsets prevent a clean single-axis progression claim.

gaps.statement: This edition has one specialised geometry result and no reviewed evidence that the same reasoning transfers across unfamiliar domains or coordinated work.
gaps.evidence_needed: Matched unseen tasks across several formal and informal domains, with held-out data, human baselines, repeated runs, and transfer tests.

gaps.statement: A simulated bar exam does not establish current knowledge, grounded truthfulness, professional judgment, multilingual depth, or group knowledge work.
gaps.evidence_needed: Dated, contamination-checked tasks with matched practitioners, source use, calibration, abstention, and consequential error review.

gaps.statement: MMMU mixes visual perception with language, knowledge, and reasoning and leaves embodied, temporal, three-dimensional, and shared perception unmeasured.
gaps.evidence_needed: Separate matched tests for recognition, spatial transformation, video, persistent scenes, embodied action, and multi-agent shared state.

gaps.statement: This edition contains no reviewed, human-calibrated observation of memory or continuity at any scope.
gaps.evidence_needed: Longitudinal tests of recall, source fidelity, commitment continuity, correction, forgetting, privacy, and transfer across sessions and agents.

gaps.statement: This edition contains no reviewed observation that separates durable learning from prompting, retrieval, context, or a newly trained model.
gaps.evidence_needed: Pre-registered before-and-after tasks showing durable change from experience, retained over time and transferred beyond trained examples.

gaps.statement: Machine-checked AlphaGeometry proofs show verifiable output, but this edition has no matched test of a system finding and repairing its own hidden errors.
gaps.evidence_needed: Blind error-seeded tasks measuring detection, calibration, repair, false alarms, and whether checks work without access to the answer.

gaps.statement: METR provides software-agent task horizons, not a measure of reliable action in physical, social, high-context, adversarial, or collective settings.
gaps.evidence_needed: Matched repeated tasks across environments and scopes, with failures, intervention load, resource use, side effects, and higher-reliability horizons reported.

gaps.statement: This edition contains no reviewed, human-calibrated observation of reciprocal coordination, conflict repair, role sharing, or collective judgment.
gaps.evidence_needed: Consent-based joint tasks with hidden information, changing roles, disagreement, handoffs, correction paths, and matched human teams.

gaps.statement: AlphaCode establishes contest program generation under tests, not novelty, value, authorship, scientific discovery, or sustained creation across scopes.
gaps.evidence_needed: Blind expert review of new artefacts and findings, independent replication or use, provenance checks, and comparisons with matched creators and teams.
